entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Tudhaliya II, also known as Tudḫaliya III in some chronologies, reigned as a pivotal Hittite Great King during the late 15th and early 14th centuries BCE, approximately from c. 1425 to c. 1390 BCE. His rule marked a critical period for the Hittite New Kingdom, characterized by the consolidation of power following a period of internal instability and external threats. He is recognized for re-establishing Hittite dominance in Anatolia and northern Syria, laying the groundwork for the empire's zenith under his successors. His reign saw significant military campaigns and diplomatic maneuvers that shaped the geopolitical landscape of the Late Bronze Age Near East, particularly against the Arzawa confederacy and the Kaska peoples.

During his tenure, Tudhaliya II confronted a formidable array of challenges, including widespread incursions from the Kaska tribes in the north, who frequently raided Hittite territories and even threatened the capital of Hattusa. He successfully campaigned to push back these barbarian incursions, securing the core Hittite lands. Simultaneously, he engaged in extensive military operations against the Arzawa confederacy in western Anatolia, a powerful rival state that challenged Hittite hegemony. His campaigns against Arzawa, though not fully conclusive, asserted Hittite influence and prevented the further fragmentation of their western frontiers. His reign also saw the construction or renovation of significant fortifications, underscoring a focus on defensive infrastructure.
